messages.content: You are BioGPT, an expert compiler architect. Translate the provided natural language biological protocol into valid, deterministic BioScript code for execution on a microfluidic biochip.

Source link: https://scispace.com/pdf/investigation-of-electrowetting-based-microfluidics-for-real-26cifb2oun.pdf
Paper DOI: N/A

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Electrowetting-Based Digital Microfluidics Coupled to Real-Time (TaqMan) PCR for Human SNP Allelic Discrimination

REAGENTS USED:
  - Allele 1 Control Template (human genomic DNA control containing allele 1 template only, targeted by the VIC-labeled probe)
  - Allele 2 Control Template (human genomic DNA control containing allele 2 template only, targeted by the FAM-labeled probe)
  - Both-Alleles Control Template (heterozygous control containing both allele 1 and allele 2 templates)
  - No-Template Control (no DNA)
  - TaqMan Allelic Discrimination Master Mix (commercially available TaqMan allelic discrimination kit reagent, ABI PN:4312559, for the C440T mutation of the CYC2C9*2 gene; contains differentially labeled FAM/VIC fluorescent probes, primers, dNTPs, and Taq polymerase; ~300 nL droplets)

STEPS:
1. For each of the four allelic controls (allele 1 only, allele 2 only, both alleles, no template), dispense a ~300 nL droplet of the control template onto the electrowetting chip.
2. Dispense a matching ~300 nL droplet of TaqMan master mix reagent for each control.
3. Actuate and merge each control droplet with its corresponding master mix droplet on the electrowetting chip to form four complete PCR reaction droplets.
4. Transport each droplet back and forth several hundred times under electrowetting control to verify standard droplet manipulations (transport, mixing, splitting, dispensing) are unaffected by the PCR reagents, then position the droplets at opposite ends of the electrode array.
5. Remove the electrowetting control voltage and thermocycle the entire chip inside the custom-built hot-air thermocycler mounted on the fluorescence microscope.
6. After each thermal cycle, read out FAM and VIC fluorescence intensity from each droplet in real time to build per-cycle amplification time-courses.
7. Discard each droplet after the thermocycling/detection run is complete.

INTERPRETATION: Successful allelic discrimination is confirmed by real-time fluorescence amplification curves showing successful DNA amplification within the droplets, and by end-point FAM/VIC intensity plots that cleanly separate droplets bearing allele 1 only, allele 2 only, both alleles, and no template, demonstrating that the addition of PCR reagents has little effect on electrowetting droplet manipulation, that the electrowetting chip environment does not inhibit PCR, and that the platform can discriminate a human SNP differing by only one base pair.

module fluorescence

manifest Allele1Control
manifest Allele2Control
manifest BothAllelesControl
manifest NoTemplateControl
manifest TaqManMasterMix

instructions:

allele1 = dispense 300 units of Allele1Control
allele2 = dispense 300 units of Allele2Control
both_alleles = dispense 300 units of BothAllelesControl
no_template = dispense 300 units of NoTemplateControl

mastermix1 = dispense 300 units of TaqManMasterMix
mastermix2 = dispense 300 units of TaqManMasterMix
mastermix3 = dispense 300 units of TaqManMasterMix
mastermix4 = dispense 300 units of TaqManMasterMix

droplet1 = mix allele1 with mastermix1 for 5s
droplet2 = mix allele2 with mastermix2 for 5s
droplet3 = mix both_alleles with mastermix3 for 5s
droplet4 = mix no_template with mastermix4 for 5s

repeat 40 times {
    heat droplet1 at 95c for 15s
    heat droplet1 at 60c for 60s
    signal1 = detect fluorescence on droplet1 for 5s

    heat droplet2 at 95c for 15s
    heat droplet2 at 60c for 60s
    signal2 = detect fluorescence on droplet2 for 5s

    heat droplet3 at 95c for 15s
    heat droplet3 at 60c for 60s
    signal3 = detect fluorescence on droplet3 for 5s

    heat droplet4 at 95c for 15s
    heat droplet4 at 60c for 60s
    signal4 = detect fluorescence on droplet4 for 5s
}

dispose droplet1
dispose droplet2
dispose droplet3
dispose droplet4

main:
	allele11[0] = dispense(Allele1Control)
	allele21[0] = dispense(Allele2Control)
	both_alleles1[0] = dispense(BothAllelesControl)
	no_template1[0] = dispense(NoTemplateControl)
	mastermix11[0] = dispense(TaqManMasterMix)
	mastermix21[0] = dispense(TaqManMasterMix)
	mastermix31[0] = dispense(TaqManMasterMix)
	mastermix41[0] = dispense(TaqManMasterMix)
	droplet11[0] = mix(allele11[0], mastermix11[0]) @ 5.0SECOND
	droplet21[0] = mix(allele21[0], mastermix21[0]) @ 5.0SECOND
	droplet31[0] = mix(both_alleles1[0], mastermix31[0]) @ 5.0SECOND
	droplet41[0] = mix(no_template1[0], mastermix41[0]) @ 5.0SECOND
bsbbr_2_h:
	PHI signal21 = {signal20,signal22}
	PHI signal41 = {signal40,signal42}
	PHI signal11 = {signal10,signal12}
	PHI REPEAT_401 = {REPEAT_400,REPEAT_402}
	PHI signal31 = {signal30,signal32}
	PHI droplet22 = {droplet21,droplet22}
	PHI droplet12 = {droplet11,droplet12}
	PHI droplet32 = {droplet31,droplet32}
	PHI droplet42 = {droplet41,droplet42}
	if REPEAT_401[0] > 0	|	true: jump bsbbr_3_t	|	false: jump bsbbr_4_f
bsbbr_3_t:
	heat(droplet12[0]) @ 95.0CELSIUS @ 15.0SECOND
	heat(droplet12[0]) @ 60.0CELSIUS @ 60.0SECOND
	signal12[0] = detect(fluorescence, droplet12[0]) @ 5.0SECOND
	heat(droplet22[0]) @ 95.0CELSIUS @ 15.0SECOND
	heat(droplet22[0]) @ 60.0CELSIUS @ 60.0SECOND
	signal22[0] = detect(fluorescence, droplet22[0]) @ 5.0SECOND
	heat(droplet32[0]) @ 95.0CELSIUS @ 15.0SECOND
	heat(droplet32[0]) @ 60.0CELSIUS @ 60.0SECOND
	signal32[0] = detect(fluorescence, droplet32[0]) @ 5.0SECOND
	heat(droplet42[0]) @ 95.0CELSIUS @ 15.0SECOND
	heat(droplet42[0]) @ 60.0CELSIUS @ 60.0SECOND
	signal42[0] = detect(fluorescence, droplet42[0]) @ 5.0SECOND
	REPEAT_402[0] = REPEAT_401[0] - 1
bsbbr_4_f:
	dispose(droplet12[0])
	dispose(droplet22[0])
	dispose(droplet32[0])
	dispose(droplet42[0])
	NOP

chemical_evidence.source_quote: Droplets (~300 nL) of complete PCR mix containing each of four allelic controls were dispensed into the chip using electrowetting ... i.e. allele 1 template only, allele 2 template only, both templates, no template
chemical_evidence.source_location: RESULTS AND DISCUSSION, second paragraph and footnote 2

chemical_evidence.source_quote: The real-time PCR reagents were obtained from a commercially available TaqMan allelic discrimination kit which contained differentially labeled (FAM/VIC) fluorescent probes corresponding to each of the two alleles.

operation_evidence.source_quote: Droplets (~300 nL) of complete PCR mix containing each of four allelic controls were dispensed into the chip using electrowetting
the addition of PCR reagents had little noticeable effect on our ability to manipulate droplets compared to standard electrolyte droplets
The droplets were then positioned at opposite ends of the array, the control voltage was removed and the entire chip was thermocycled.

Fluorescence time-courses revealed successful amplification of DNA within the droplets and sufficient specificity was obtained in order to permit discrimination of alleles differing in only one base pair

numeric_mismatches.note: The paper states only that 'the entire chip was thermocycled' without specifying per-step temperatures or hold times. 95C denaturation / 60C combined anneal-extend is the standard TaqMan two-temperature qPCR profile, used here as a reasonable assumption rather than a value stated in the paper.
The paper does not state an explicit cycle count; the number of cycles is assumed from the ~0-50 cycle axis range shown in Fig. 2's amplification time-course.

numeric_mismatches.field: PCR reagent vs. 0.1 M KCl electrolyte comparison (first key issue)
numeric_mismatches.note: Not modeled. This is a droplet-manipulation-compatibility comparison, not part of the PCR reaction/detection sequence itself.

numeric_mismatches.field: cross-contamination experiment (Fig. 3, 5,000 flow cycles / 15,000 electrode transfers, off-chip conventional real-time PCR readout)
numeric_mismatches.note: Not modeled. This is a separate validation sub-experiment using a conventional (non-electrowetting) PCR instrument for final readout, outside the scope of the core on-chip assay translation.

metadata.notes: This protocol details Electrowetting-Based Digital Microfluidics Coupled to Real-Time (TaqMan) PCR for Human SNP Allelic Discrimination. The assay is performed on a Digital Microfluidics (DMF) platform. Key reagents used in the assay include Allele 1 Control Template and Allele 2 Control Template.
